note: Window agent p0600-p0699, 1-2 Nov 2026. 6 events, 10 keyframe overrides, 2 rulings; every entry rests on a page opened in that run (see each source and why).

region.text: the 1,278 cells of Chita and Buryatia (Transbaikal) that Cliopatria's Tang shape of 647-681 draws as direct Tang land

events.note: 647: the Yanran protectorate founded; the Anbei page has it 'controlled the Mongolian Plateau from 647 to 682' and its territory 'extended from Lake Baikal to the north'. The Tang shape of 647-681 still draws the Transbaikal cells (Chita, Buryatia) as direct land; this puts them under the protectorate's vassal tint with the plateau (the same relation as the dossier's own 647 event).

region.text: the restoration's land beyond Juryu, lost by 662

events.note: 662: the movement is reduced to Juryu. 'By 662, they were in serious trouble, and their area of control was confined to the fortress of Churyu'. This replaces the dossier's ledger/1, which is skipped because the gazetteer does not know 'Seocheon'; the land goes to the Ungjin Commandery, 'created in place of Baekje' (660-671).

region.text: Juryu (Churyu), 'in modern Seocheon County, South Chungcheong' (the gazetteer does not know Seocheon; Gunsan, on the opposite bank of the Geum estuary, 30 km, stands for it)

events.note: October 663: Juryu falls after Baekgang (27-28 August 663 lunar; 4-5 October Julian) and the restoration movement is 'crush[ed]'. The Ungjin Commandery 'existed between 660 and 671' 'in place of Baekje', so the last rebel patch becomes commandery land. This replaces the dossier's ledger/2 and its successor land, skipped because 'Seocheon' is not in the gazetteer (otherwise Baekje's land is ownerless 663-671).

region.text: the Ashina buffer state between the Yellow River and the Gobi

events.note: 645: the buffer state ends with the Tang reconquest. Eastern Turkic Khaganate page infobox: 'Buffer state of the Tang dynasty (639-645)' and 'Reconquest by Tang dynasty: 645'. The dossier's vassal_end of 645 hands the whole vassal land (4,431 cells of Inner Mongolia) to nobody until the Tang keyframe of 647; this puts it under direct Tang rule at once.

region.text: Swabia (Alamannia): the 241 cells the Frankish dossier's own 644 loss releases (Cliopatria's 'Frisia Kingdom' shape of 644 inside the Frankish shape of 641)

events.note: 644: Alamannia is independent of the Franks. Alamannia page: 'After the death of Dagobert I in 638' Alamannia 'broke its ties with its Frankish sovereigns and struggled for independence', 'largely successful until the early 8th century'. The Frankish dossier's ledger/24 releases these 241 Swabian cells in 644 to 'frisia-kingdom', a Cliopatria label with no dossier, so they have been ownerless from 644 to the end of the window (and in the dossiers' later years); this gives them to the Duchy of Alamannia, whose own keyframe (496-723, the Lake Constance and Upper Danube land) already describes them. The year 644 is the Frankish dossier's; the page gives 638 as the break.

the Sui cities south of the Qinling that Li Xiaogong brought over: 'modern southern Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Chongqing' (the page names no boundary; the Hanzhong circle is the researcher's reading of southern Shaanxi, and the region is cut to Cliopatria's 623 Tang outline, which stops at the basin edge)

correction.text: Guanzhong (Chang'an, occupied in winter 617) and the Fen valley around Taiyuan, where Li Yuan had been governor: the Tang at its proclamation on 18 June 618; plus the Sui cities of southern Shaanxi, Sichuan and Chongqing that Li Xiaogong brought over (winter 617 - spring 618)

keyframe_overrides.why: The 618 keyframe (Guanzhong and Shanxi only) snaps away the 1,443 Sichuan, Chongqing and Hanzhong cells that the dossier's own 618 gain event gave the Tang, leaving them ownerless until the 623 snap. Emperor Gaozu page: 'Li Xiaogong was able to persuade the Sui cities in modern southern Shaanxi, Sichuan, and Chongqing to submit', placed after the capture of Chang'an (winter 617) and before Emperor Yang's death (spring 618).

correction.text: as drawn without the Levant remnants; Egypt stays Roman until the Persians take Alexandria in June 619 (ledger 619, 621)

keyframe_overrides.why: The 617 correction also subtracts Egypt, which empties its 2,008 cells from 617 to 622 (the ledger loss of 619 then has nothing to move, and the Sasanian shape fills Egypt only in 623). Sasanian conquest of Egypt page: 'The Persian invasion of Egypt began either in 617 or 618'; 'Alexandria was then betrayed to the Persians by a certain Peter in June 619'; 'by 621, the province was securely in Persian hands'.

correction.text: 692: the 692 shape minus Morocco, Fars, Kerman, Caucasian Albania and Iberia, Cyrenaica, Najd, Bahrain, Oman, Yemen and Ta'if; and without Algeria, which the caliphate gets only with the ledger's later gains (the Kahina's Numidia c. 701, Altava 708)

keyframe_overrides.why: The Cliopatria shape draws the whole Algerian Tell and Sahara (about 2,900 cells, taking Altava's Oranais from its 690 keyframe) as caliphate land from 692. The Maghreb page has the Arabs hold Kairouan and Ifriqiya (Kairouan founded 670, lost to Kusaila 683, retaken 688/9), Carthage only in 695/6-698 ('ending the Byzantine presence by 698'), the Kahina in the eastern Aures slain 'around 701', and Musa ibn Nusayr's conquest of the west 'in 708' with the whole Maghreb done in 709; it says nothing of an Umayyad hold on western or Saharan Algeria before then. The dossier's own note at 692 records the same overreach as 'not corrected'.

region.text: Cyrenaica (Barqa) only: Tripoli 'had fallen back into the hands of the Byzantines soon after Amr ibn al-Aas' departure' (Maghreb page, at 647)

rulings.why: Maghreb page: after Alexandria 'Barqa fell without opposition' (c. 642-643) and 'Amr returned to Fustat, leaving Uqba ibn Nafi as Governor of Barqa'; Barqa stayed Arab until a Byzantine fleet landed in Cyrenaica in 690 ('Barqa had fallen out of Muslim control'). The Byzantine 656 keyframe still draws Cyrenaica (378 cells) as Byzantine for 656-660. [Reviewer, 2026-11-02: region narrowed from Libya to Cyrenaica, because the page has Tripoli back in Byzantine hands soon after 643; the cells settled are unchanged.]

Maghreb page: Barqa was Arab until 'Barqa had fallen out of Muslim control' in 690; Uqba took Ghadames in 662 and, with Shurayk, Labda (Leptis Magna) in 663, then Waddan in the Fezzan; in 666/7 raids went out 'via Tripoli - now emerging as a centre for Muslim naval forces' while 'Uqba ibn Nafi was campaigning in Sirte, Fezzan'. The Byzantine 666 keyframe gives back 163 cells of the Tripolitanian coast (from Sirte to the Tunisian border, Tripoli included) that were Arab-held. [Reviewer, 2026-11-02: why corrected to the cells the ruling settles and the page's Tripoli sentence.]
